title: A concrete quotient-cone model for the canonical scalar-extension pullback comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$, $A_{F,m}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m$ and $B_{F,W,m}=(A_{F,m})_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. The canonical $R_W$-module $S_W$ is finite free. Write $C_WH=H\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ and $T_WH$ for integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], with its specified natural completion comparison $\chi_{W,H}:C_WH\to T_WH$ on derived-complete $H$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison].

Let $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and put $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$. Then $Q$ is flat-term K-flat over $S_Y$ and represents $C_YK$. Define
$$P_{E,m}=P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{E,Y,m},\qquad Q_{L,m}=Q\otimes_{S_Y}B_{L,Y,m}=P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{L,Y,m}.$$
Here $R_Y\to B_{L,Y,m}$ is precisely the same-index map $\rho_m=(\iota_m)_Y\pi^E_m$ of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], with $\iota_m:A_{E,m}\to A_{L,m}$.
For $F=E,L$ and a flat-term K-flat complex $M$ over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}$, put
$$D^F_m(M)=\operatorname{Res}^F_m g_{F,m}^*(M\otimes B_{F,Y,m}),\qquad A_F(M)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_mD^F_m(M)\to\prod_mD^F_m(M))[-1],$$
where $g_{F,m}^*$ is finite module pullback and $s$ is induced by quotient transitions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Thus $A_E(P)$ represents $Lg_E^*K$, and $A_L(Q)$ represents $Lg_L^*(C_YK)$.

There is a specified map of strict towers of $S_X$-complexes
$$d_m:D^E_m(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\longrightarrow D^L_m(Q).$$
It is the change-of-rings map induced by $P_{E,m}\to Q_{L,m}$, $p\otimes\bar a\mapsto p\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)$, by the coefficient structure maps of $g^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and by $S_X\to B_{L,X,m}$. Equivalently, on local tensor generators its formula is
$$((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s\longmapsto (g^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)))\otimes\bigl(\iota_m(b)\pi^L_m(s)\bigr),$$
where $\bar a$ is a local section of $B_{E,Y,m}$ inside inverse image, $b$ of $B_{E,X,m}$, and $s$ of $S_X$. Tensor products mean sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].
Since $S_X$ is finite free, the canonical tensor/product maps identify $A_E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X$ with the Roos cone of $D^E_\bullet(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X$. Let
$$\delta_P:A_E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\longrightarrow A_L(Q)$$
be the resulting cone map induced by $d_\bullet$; on cone coordinates it is $(b,a)\mapsto((\prod_m d_m)b,(\prod_m d_m)a)$ after these canonical tensor/product identifications. In particular both coordinates are specified.

Let $B(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mQ_{L,m}\to\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mQ_{L,m})[-1]$, representing $T_YK$. The chain map
$$\chi_Y(P):Q\to B(P),\quad q\mapsto(0,(q\bmod\varpi_L^m)_m)$$
represents $\chi_{Y,K}$ and is a quasi-isomorphism. The map $\delta_P$ is a quasi-isomorphism and the canonical tensor-and-completion scalar-extension comparison is the following specified derived morphism:
$$\alpha_K=Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})\circ[\delta_P]\circ\chi_{X,Lg_E^*K}^{-1}:T_X(Lg_E^*K)\longrightarrow Lg_L^*(T_YK).$$
All identifications here are the canonical resolution comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]; the formula is independent of $P$ and natural in $K$. It specifies the canonical comparison described by ordinary tensor associativity and strict quotient-tower completion in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between its two objects. The brackets denote localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: Set R_W=R-hat and S_W=S-hat. The finite-free completed scalar comparison says S_W is finite free over R_W and identifies ordinary derived tensor with the specified strict-tower scalar extension on derived-complete inputs. Choose the flat-term K-flat resolution P -> K and put Q=P tensor_{R_Y} S_Y. Derived change of rings and K-flat change of rings show that Q represents C_Y K and is K-flat with flat terms over S_Y.

The coefficient inclusion gives compatible maps rho_m=(iota_m)_Y pi^E_m and hence P_{E,m}=P tensor B_{E,Y,m} and Q_{L,m}=Q tensor B_{L,Y,m}=P tensor B_{L,Y,m}. The last equality is tensor associativity and balancing. The strict-tower definition of integral scalar extension and the finite-level pullback definition give exactly the towers used in A_E(P) and A_L(Q).

proof.text: The definition of the integral derived operations is the Roos cone Cone(1-s: product_m Res^F_m g_{F,m}^*(M tensor B_{F,Y,m}) -> product_m Res^F_m g_{F,m}^*(M tensor B_{F,Y,m}))[-1]. Applying it to (F,M)=(E,P) and (L,Q) gives A_E(P) and A_L(Q), which represent Lg_E^* K and Lg_L^*(C_Y K) by the K-flat resolution and well-definedness results.

At level m, tensor balancing and iota_m define d_m:D^E_m(P) tensor_{R_X} S_X -> D^L_m(Q). On local pure tensors the formula is ((g^{-1}(p tensor a-bar)) tensor b) tensor s maps to (g^{-1}(p tensor iota_m(a-bar))) tensor (iota_m(b) pi^L_m(s)). The inverse-image coefficient map and sheaf tensor product make this formula respect differentials, balancing, and quotient transitions, so the d_m form a strict tower map.

proof.text: Since S_X is finite free over R_X, tensoring with S_X commutes with the termwise countable products in the Roos cone; in a finite free basis this is a finite direct-sum calculation. It also commutes with 1-s and the shifted cone. Applying the cone construction to the tower map gives delta_P:A_E(P) tensor_{R_X} S_X -> A_L(Q), with both coordinates (b,a) mapped to ((product_m d_m)b,(product_m d_m)a).

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1 and finite-free product/cone calculation in Lemma 6.8.2(1)

proof.text: The finite-free completed scalar comparison at Y is represented on Q by chi_Y(P): q maps to (0,(q mod varpi_L^m)_m) in the Roos cone. Its shifted-product component is zero by the cone convention, and the comparison theorem says it is a quasi-isomorphism for derived-complete inputs. Thus it represents chi_{Y,K}:C_Y K -> T_Y K and is invertible in the derived category.

Let $e$ be the ramification index, so that $\varpi_E\mathcal O_L=\varpi_L^e\mathcal O_L$ and $A_{E,m}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_E^m\mathcal O_L=A_{L,em}$. Level identification. Apply the completed-constant-sheaf reduction theorem to $(\mathcal O_E,(\varpi_E))$ and to $(\mathcal O_L,(\varpi_L))$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$: $R_X$ and $S_X$ are flat over the constant sheaves $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, $\underline{\mathcal O_L}$, and $R_X\otimes_{\underline{\mathcal O_E}}\underline{A_{E,m}}\cong(A_{E,m})_X$, $S_X\otimes_{\underline{\mathcal O_L}}\underline{A_{L,a}}\cong(A_{L,a})_X$ by the reduction maps. Hence, constant sheaves commuting with tensor products, $(A_{E,m})_X\otimes_{R_X}S_X\cong\underline{A_{E,m}}\otimes_{\underline{\mathcal O_E}}S_X\cong\underline{A_{L,em}}\otimes_{\underline{\mathcal O_L}}S_X\cong(A_{L,em})_X$. Since $D^E_m(P)$ is restricted from an $(A_{E,m})_X$-module complex, tensor associativity and base change of the module pullback $g_{E,m}^*$ along $A_{E,m}\to A_{L,em}$ give a canonical isomorphism $\tilde d_m:D^E_m(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\cong D^L_{em}(Q)$, compatible with transitions, under which the statement's $d_m$ (induced by $\iota_m$, which factors as $A_{E,m}\to A_{L,em}\to A_{L,m}$) is the composite L-transition $T_{m,em}:D^L_{em}(Q)\to D^L_m(Q)$. It need not be injective (e.g. $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $L=\mathbf Q_\ell(\sqrt\ell)$, $e=2$, $m=1$). Thus, writing $Y_n=D^L_n(Q)$, $K_\bullet=(Y_n)$ and $K^{(e)}_\bullet=(Y_{en})$, $\delta_P$ becomes the cone map $\Delta=\mathsf R(T):\mathsf R(K^{(e)}_\bullet)\to\mathsf R(K_\bullet)$ applying $T=\prod_nT_{n,en}$ to both coordinates. Cofinality. The cofinality lemma applies with $A=\mathbf Z$: modules over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,X}$ have the same kernels, cokernels and (sectionwise) countable products as their underlying abelian sheaves, these products are exact by the countable-products theorem, and the coordinate and block maps are $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,X}$-linear. It gives the quasi-isomorphism $r_e:\mathsf R(K_\bullet)\to\mathsf R(K^{(e)}_\bullet)$, $r_e(y,x)=(b_ey,a_ex)$ on cone coordinates. Coordinate check. $\Delta r_e(y,x)=(\psi y,\varphi x)$ with $\varphi(x)_n=T_{n,en}x_{en}$ and $\psi(y)_n=\sum_{i=en}^{e(n+1)-1}T_{n,i}y_i$. Put $h(y)_n=\sum_{i=n}^{en-1}T_{n,i}y_i$ (zero for $e=1$) and $f=1-s$. Telescoping gives $h f=1-\varphi$ and $f h=1-\psi$. Hence $H(y,x)=(0,hy)$ satisfies $dH+Hd=(fh,hf)=1-\Delta r_e$ on the cone (up to the sign of the $[-1]$ shift), so $\Delta r_e$ is homotopic to the identity. As $r_e$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $\Delta$, hence $\delta_P$, is a quasi-isomorphism, and $[\delta_P]=[r_e]^{-1}$ under the identifications $\tilde d$. Conclusion. The finite-free completion comparison makes $\chi_{Y,K}$ invertible (K is derived complete). The isomorphism theorem for $g$ gives $Lg_E^*K\cong g^{-1}K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ for the same integral pullback (def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom uses def-pur-integral-derived-operations at integral level), so $Lg_E^*K$ is derived complete and $\chi_{X,Lg_E^*K}$ is invertible. Hence $\alpha_K=Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})\circ[\delta_P]\circ\chi_{X,Lg_E^*K}^{-1}$ is a composite of isomorphisms $T_X(Lg_E^*K)\to Lg_L^*(T_YK)$. The scalar-extension theorem asserts only the existence of a natural isomorphism between these objects; $\alpha_K$ is such an isomorphism (naturality in Step 8), built from exactly the ingredients its route uses (ordinary tensor associativity, the quotient-tower completion maps and the $e$-subsequence reindexing), and the statement designates this composite as the specified comparison.

proof.text: All maps in the construction are induced by functorial coefficient and inverse-image maps, tensor balancing, products, cones, and the explicit quotient reductions. The well-definedness theorem identifies these maps after replacing P by any other flat-term K-flat resolution, so the localized morphism is independent of P. The same coordinate formulas commute with morphisms of K, and the block maps in the cofinality lemma compose under successive index reindexing; ordinary tensor associativity gives the successive coefficient-extension identity. The completion comparisons are natural by the finite-free comparison. Thus the displayed formula is natural in K and is the specified canonical comparison, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between its source and target.
